## Observed Facts

- **KERNEL is the largest component by volume.** It has 4,324,651 of 4,747,963 Log Entries (about 91%) in BGL, with no time or level filter [E1].
- **KERNEL also has the most FATAL entries.** It has 626,450 of 855,195 FATAL Log Entries (about 73%) [E2].
- **APP is the second concern.** It has 228,536 Log Entries [E1], and all 228,536 are FATAL [E2].
- **Smaller components with FATAL entries:** LINKCARD has 206 FATAL Log Entries [E2], and MMCS has 3 [E2]. DISCOVERY, HARDWARE, and MONITOR have no FATAL entries in the grouped results [E1, E2].

Data Scope for all counts: Dataset BGL, full time range, no text, component, or level filter. The counts are Log Entries, not incidents.

## Hypotheses

- KERNEL is the most likely biggest risk by measured frequency. It leads on both total volume and FATAL volume, so it is the component to look at first.
- APP is a close second for severity. Every APP entry is FATAL, which may matter more per entry even though its volume is much lower.

## Unknowns

- The logs do not show whether these FATAL entries cause outages, lost work, or customer impact. I cannot state that.
- I did not check the time trend. I do not know whether KERNEL's FATAL volume is steady, growing, or from a single spike.
- Log Entries are not incidents. The logs do not show how many distinct incidents produced the KERNEL or APP entries.

## Next Step

Run a trend on KERNEL FATAL entries by day to see whether the volume is recurring or a one-off burst. If it is recurring, the next step is to group KERNEL FATAL entries by alert tag to find the most common failure type.
